title: Johnny Desmond, Ray Biondi, Graham Young and the trumpet section
summary: Roy fondly recalls band friends including Ray Biondi, Graham Young, Joe Giuscara and Norman Murphy.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I forgot to mention one of the greatest cats in there was Johnny Desmond. He was beautiful. And also Ray Everett. Those two cats I got along great with, you know, and there was no underhand things any kind of way. You see, I'm very sensitive to those things. You know, word gets
around... See, a cat will laugh and grin with you, but then he'll make a mistake of saying something to other people, and then it gets back to you, you know. That's how I know.

Then I can tell by actions, too. Like, Ray would... If I had to stay across the tracks, he'd go and stay across the tracks with me. Nobody else would do that. Poor Ray died, too. I'm talking about Ray Biondi. That thing when Gene got arrested then... Well, Ray was in the middle of all that, you know. Ray was right there. Yeah, I liked that cat, man.

And Graham Young. He was here. He was right here before ...(?)... I knew his mother very well, because she used to always come by and see me. She was a nice lady. She played piano. He's doing very good, Graham Young. He's got him a nice boat, and his kids are all married. He's doin' real nice. I just got a call from him. He said him and his wife just climbed the Great Wall of China -- they were in China.
No, Joe Giuscara(?) was lead. It was Joe, Ray, Graham and myself. He played lead on a lot of things. He was a good trumpet player. And he could play my things
very good. He used to play... I have a... What did he used to play of mine? Oh, this arrangement they had on "Blues In The Night." He could really play the hell out of that.
Oh, another cat who used to be in that band I liked, too -- Norman Murphy. I just got a call from... You know, Norman had a heart attack, too.
He wrote me a letter, he said, 'It's not bad enough that I tried to play like you, but then I had to go and try to have a heart attack!' I owe him a letter. I've got to write him, too, you know.
